name: FrontierLLM Constitution
description: An open constitution for frontier large-language-model development — pretraining, fine-tuning, evaluation, serving and agentic tooling — expressed as ordinary and absolute provisions in the sense of Chapter 5, Definition 1 of the Digital Judiciary programme. Provisions carry a status: in_force, deferred, or advisory. A provision that is not in force may never be absolute.
status_note: A deferred provision is enacted but not yet applicable; an advisory provision names suggested actions rather than obligations. Neither may be marked absolute, and the build refuses a constitution in which one is.

authorities.disjointness: A1: the three classes are pairwise disjoint over the deployment lifetime.

standing_declaration.note: A9 first limb. This corpus declares that a party holds contest standing adverse to grants, namely the safety evaluation officer, so that the N-standing cases can exercise both postures. A deployment must replace this with its own fact.

provisions.family_title: Child safety: abuse-material detection, age assurance and minors' data
provisions.title: Child sexual abuse material detection on uploads, generations and model outputs, and the CyberTipline report and preservation path, are never disabled, sampled down or made configurable
provisions.citation: 18 U.S.C. §2258A as amended by the REPORT Act (Pub. L. 118-59, 7 May 2024: one-year preservation, expanded reportable conduct); 18 U.S.C. §2252A; NIST AI 600-1 §2.10 obscene, degrading and abusive content
provisions.source_status: US statute, public domain. Absolute because §2258A(a) is a mandatory reporting duty with criminal penalties for knowing and wilful failure (§2258A(e)); no one below the legislature may accept the risk. The EU AI Act Art. 5 limb on AI-generated CSAM added by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 is in transition to 2 Dec 2026 and is noted, not relied on

provisions.family_title: Transparency, content provenance, documentation and incident reporting
provisions.title: Machine-readable synthetic-content marking on every generative output modality is never removed, made opt-out per tenant or stripped by a downstream stage the provider controls
provisions.citation: EU AI Act Art. 50(2) (applicable from 2 Aug 2026); Commission Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content; California SB 942 (AI Transparency Act) as amended by AB 853 (operative 2 Aug 2026) latent disclosures; C2PA content-credentials specification, identifier only
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable; in force for systems placed on the market from 2 Aug 2026, with the Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 grace period to 2 Dec 2026 for systems already on the market — this pack's releases are new placements. SB 942/AB 853 public domain (under EO 14365 preemption challenge). Absolute because Art. 50(2) admits no proportionality defence and marking removed at source cannot be restored downstream

provisions.family_title: Transparency, content provenance, documentation and incident reporting
provisions.title: General-purpose model technical documentation, downstream-provider information and the public training-content summary are current at release, not carried over from the previous one
provisions.citation: EU AI Act Art. 53(1)(a)–(d) with Annexes XI and XII (applicable 2 Aug 2025; Commission enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026); Commission training-content summary template (July 2025); GPAI Code of Practice Transparency chapter Model Documentation Form
provisions.source_status: EU text, template and Commission-hosted Code reusable under 2011/833/EU. Ordinary because a documentation gap is correctable after the fact and Art. 53(2) carves out open-source models below systemic risk

provisions.family_title: Transparency, content provenance, documentation and incident reporting
provisions.title: The frontier transparency report is published at or before deployment, and the anonymous internal safety-concern channel is preserved with its anti-retaliation notice
provisions.citation: California SB 53 (Transparency in Frontier AI Act, signed 29 Sept 2025, eff. 1 Jan 2026) — transparency report and frontier AI framework (Bus. & Prof. Code §22757.12), whistleblower protections (Lab. Code §1107 et seq.); Directive (EU) 2019/1937 whistleblower protection; GPAI Code of Practice Measure 8.3
provisions.source_status: California statute; public domain. Under the federal preemption challenge opened by EO 14365 (11 Dec 2025); section pins directionally supported, not verified. Ordinary because the report duty attaches at deployment and is remediable; the channel duty is real but the statute names the employer, not a code path, as the obligor

provisions.family_title: Transparency, content provenance, documentation and incident reporting
provisions.title: Critical safety incident detection signals reach the reporting queue, and the statutory reporting clock is fixed in code, never configurable, extended or avoided by severity defaults
provisions.citation: California SB 53 critical safety incident reporting to Cal OES within 15 days, 24 hours where imminent risk of death or serious injury (Bus. & Prof. Code §22757.13); EU AI Act Art. 55(1)(c) (serious incidents to the AI Office without undue delay); GPAI Code of Practice Safety and Security chapter, Commitment 9
provisions.source_status: California statute; public domain. Under the federal preemption challenge opened by EO 14365 (11 Dec 2025); section pins directionally supported, not verified; EU text reusable and binding since 2 Aug 2025 independent of the state law. Absolute because a statutory notification clock is set by the legislature and no operator may lengthen it; the provision governs the clock's configurability, not the reporting act (which FL-SF-007 already covers)

provisions.family_title: User harm: crisis safety, persuasion, high-stakes advice, companion use and abuse
provisions.title: The crisis and self-harm safety classifier and its crisis-resource handoff are never weakened, bypassed for streaming or removed from a consumer response path
provisions.citation: California SB 243 companion-chatbot protocol for suicidal ideation and crisis referral (Bus. & Prof. Code §22601 et seq., eff. 1 Jan 2026); New York Gen. Bus. Law Art. 47 companion-AI safeguards (eff. 5 Nov 2025); NIST AI 600-1 §2.7 human–AI configuration; EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(b) exploitation of vulnerability
provisions.source_status: State statutes public domain, under EO 14365 preemption challenge; EU Art. 5 reusable and in force. Absolute as a safety floor: the harm is irreversible and the protocol duty is set by statute, so a release owner cannot accept the risk to clear false positives

provisions.family_title: User harm: crisis safety, persuasion, high-stakes advice, companion use and abuse
provisions.title: Political-persuasion and election-influence policy checks run for every tenant, and the election-integrity classifier stays in the release gate through an electoral cycle
provisions.citation: Regulation (EU) 2024/900 on transparency and targeting of political advertising (applicable 10 Oct 2025); EU AI Act Art. 50(4) deepfake and public-interest text disclosure; Digital Services Act Arts. 34–35 (systemic risks to electoral processes); NIST AI 600-1 §2.8 information integrity
provisions.source_status: EU texts reusable and in force; NIST public domain and advisory. Ordinary because the persuasion threshold is a policy parameter the governance board sets; the floor is that the check exists and applies uniformly

provisions.family_title: User harm: crisis safety, persuasion, high-stakes advice, companion use and abuse
provisions.title: High-stakes medical, legal and financial responses keep their qualified-professional handoff and their automated-assistant disclosure in every served persona
provisions.citation: Utah Artificial Intelligence Policy Act, Utah Code §13-72-101 et seq. (disclosure in regulated occupations, as amended 2025); FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45) deception authority; EU AI Act Art. 50(1) interaction disclosure; Illinois Wellness and Oversight for Psychological Resources Act (2025)
provisions.source_status: Utah code section renumbering and Illinois act text directionally supported, not verified; FTC Act and EU text in force. State instruments under EO 14365 preemption challenge

provisions.family_title: User harm: crisis safety, persuasion, high-stakes advice, companion use and abuse
provisions.title: Companion-mode safeguards for accounts flagged as minors — periodic break reminders, sexual-content blocking and an explicit non-human disclosure — are enforced and not persona-configurable
provisions.citation: California SB 243 (Bus. & Prof. Code §22601 et seq.: three-hour break reminders and sexual-content restrictions for minors); New York Gen. Bus. Law Art. 47; FTC Section 6(b) inquiry into AI companions (Sept 2025); NIST AI 600-1 §2.7 emotional entanglement
provisions.source_status: State statutes public domain, under EO 14365 preemption challenge; FTC 6(b) inquiry is advisory signal only. Ordinary because the reminder cadence and blocking scope are parameters the policy board may set within the statute

provisions.family_title: User harm: crisis safety, persuasion, high-stakes advice, companion use and abuse
provisions.title: The usage-policy enforcement and abuse-monitoring pipeline runs at its declared sample rate on every tier, and non-consensual intimate imagery removal completes within the statutory clock
provisions.citation: TAKE IT DOWN Act (Pub. L. 119-12, 19 May 2025; 48-hour notice-and-removal, platform compliance from 19 May 2026); EU AI Act Art. 55(1)(b) systemic-risk mitigation; Digital Services Act Art. 16 notice-and-action; GPAI Code of Practice Measure 5 (safety mitigations, usage monitoring)
provisions.source_status: US statute public domain; EU texts reusable. Ordinary because the sample rate is a governed parameter; the 48-hour removal clock is statutory and a change that made it configurable would engage S-04 through FL-TR-004's reasoning

provisions.family_title: Privacy operations: erasure, retention commitments, tenant isolation, workers and lawful access
provisions.title: Erasure and unlearning requests propagate to training manifests, derived corpora and the next-run exclusion list, and complete within the statutory window
provisions.citation: GDPR Art. 17 with Art. 12(3) (one month, extendable with notice) and Art. 17(2) downstream notification; EDPB Opinion 28/2024 (unlawful development taints deployment unless the model is demonstrably anonymous)
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable; EDPB opinion licence unverified, paraphrased. Ordinary because Art. 17(3) carries exemptions and the technical remedy against trained weights is unsettled; the floor is propagation, not retraining

provisions.family_title: Privacy operations: erasure, retention commitments, tenant isolation, workers and lawful access
provisions.title: Zero-data-retention commitments are enforced in the retention code path itself, with no debug capture and no service-level override flag
provisions.citation: GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation and Art. 28(3)(a) processing on documented instructions; customer data-processing agreements as the source of the commitment
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable; the zero-retention term itself is contractual, stated as a parameter. Ordinary because the privacy office may vary the commitment by contract; the floor is that code, not configuration, carries it

provisions.family_title: Privacy operations: erasure, retention commitments, tenant isolation, workers and lawful access
provisions.title: Prefix and key-value caches, fine-tune adapters and retrieval indexes are partitioned per tenant and never shared, loadable or queryable across a tenant boundary
provisions.citation: GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) and Art. 32 (integrity, confidentiality, security of processing); Art. 33–34 (a cross-tenant disclosure is a personal-data breach); EU AI Act Art. 55(1)(d) cybersecurity of the model and infrastructure
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable and in force. Absolute because a cross-tenant read is a notifiable breach on first occurrence and a disclosure of one customer's confidential data to another; there is no risk owner with standing to accept it on the disclosed tenant's behalf

provisions.family_title: Privacy operations: erasure, retention commitments, tenant isolation, workers and lawful access
provisions.title: Annotator and data-worker personal data is processed under a recorded basis, stripped from exported preference datasets, and the workers' graphic-content exposure limits stay enforced in the queue
provisions.citation: GDPR Art. 88 (employment context) and Art. 32; Directive (EU) 2024/2831 on platform work (transposition by 2 Dec 2026 — deferred, noted); Partnership on AI Responsible Sourcing of Data Enrichment Services guidelines (advisory)
provisions.source_status: EU text reusable and in force for the GDPR limbs; the Platform Work Directive is deferred until transposition and is cited as context, not relied on; PAI guidance advisory

provisions.family_title: Privacy operations: erasure, retention commitments, tenant isolation, workers and lawful access
provisions.title: Government and law-enforcement requests for user data pass legal review before disclosure, are logged append-only with their scope, and trigger customer notice where the law allows
provisions.citation: Stored Communications Act, 18 U.S.C. §§2702–2703; CLOUD Act, 18 U.S.C. §2713; GDPR Art. 48 (transfers or disclosures not authorised by Union law); EU–US Data Privacy Framework adequacy decision (10 July 2023)
provisions.source_status: US statute public domain; EU text reusable. Ordinary because disclosure without notice is lawful under a non-disclosure order and legal review may lawfully approve; the floor is that review and logging happen

scenario_catalogue.note: Every provision carries `scenarios` (ids from constitution/scenarios.json) and `harm_classes` (computed from the catalogue, never authored per provision). harness/coverage.py and VC-50 compute coverage from the executed corpus.
